subtopic: Variable Life Insurance Fees and Expenses
source_evidence: You will pay several ongoing and transaction-based fees and expenses when you invest in a variable life insurance policy. These fees and expenses may be significant and will reduce the value of your account.
answer: Variable life insurance can involve multiple types of fees. Common examples include ongoing mortality and expense charges, cost-of-insurance and administration fees, sales fees deducted from premiums, and fees for transactions or optional benefits. You may also pay fees charged by the underlying investment funds, loan interest if you borrow, or a surrender charge if you surrender the policy or withdraw money during the charge period. These costs reduce account value and may mean you need to pay additional premiums to keep the policy from lapsing. Review the policy prospectus and ask which charges apply, how they are calculated, and when they are charged.
